sources: asc_visiting
https://www.gov.uk/guidance/supporting-safer-visiting-in-care-homes-during-infectious-illness-outbreaks
UKHSA safer visiting guidance for care homes
proportionate visiting decisions during infectious illness outbreaks
The guidance states that visits should normally continue with proportionate precautions.
Any exceptional reduction in visiting should be risk-based, time-limited and documented.
asc_ppe_landing
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppe-guide-for-non-aerosol-generating-procedures
DHSC non-AGP PPE guide publication
selection, donning and doffing of PPE for non-aerosol-generating adult social care tasks
The publication covers PPE for droplet precautions and standard infection-control procedures.
It links both printable and text-only donning and doffing instructions.
asc_ppe_detail
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppe-guide-for-non-aerosol-generating-procedures/guide-to-donning-putting-on-and-doffing-removing-ppe-non-agp-in-adult-social-care-settings-text-only-version
DHSC detailed non-AGP PPE instructions
safe sequence for putting on and removing PPE in adult social care
The instructions require hand cleaning before donning and repeatedly during doffing.
Glove use is based on risk of exposure to blood or body fluids rather than routine use.
asc_mdro
https://www.gov.uk/guidance/infection-prevention-and-control-for-multidrug-resistant-organisms-in-adult-social-care-settings
UKHSA adult social care MDRO guidance
prevention of transmission of multidrug-resistant organisms in adult social care
The guidance covers MDRO transmission and IPC for adult social care staff and managers.
It includes MRSA, VRE, CPE and Candidozyma auris as examples relevant to England.
prison_ipc_landing
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/infection-control-in-prisons-and-places-of-detention
UKHSA adult prison IPC publication
infection prevention and reduction of infection-related harm in adult prisons
The publication is for managers and staff in HMP and non-HMP adult prison settings.
The guidance was rebranded and updated by UKHSA in January 2026.
prison_ipc_detail
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/infection-control-in-prisons-and-places-of-detention/infection-prevention-and-control-guidelines-for-adult-prisons
UKHSA detailed adult prison IPC guidance
standard and transmission-based precautions adapted to adult prison environments
The guidance applies standard precautions to all staff and people in prison.
It addresses hand hygiene, PPE, respiratory hygiene, cleaning, waste, linen and infection-specific measures.
prison_ari

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/acute-respiratory-illness-including-flu-and-covid-19-in-prisons/flu-and-acute-respiratory-illness-ari-in-prisons-and-other-prescribed-places-of-detention-ppds
UKHSA prison acute respiratory infection guidance
management of flu, COVID-19 and other ARIs in prisons and prescribed detention settings
The guidance covers infection prevention, case management and outbreak control for ARIs in detention settings.
It specifies hand and respiratory hygiene, environmental disinfection and risk-based masking.
hsca_ipc_code

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-health-and-social-care-act-2008-code-of-practice-on-the-prevention-and-control-of-infections-and-related-guidance/health-and-social-care-act-2008-code-of-practice-on-the-prevention-and-control-of-infections-and-related-guidance
DHSC Health and Social Care Act IPC code
registered-provider compliance with infection prevention and cleanliness requirements
The code describes what registered providers should do to comply with infection-control requirements.
It links effective IPC, cleanliness and prudent antimicrobial stewardship to safe care.
outbreak_toolkit6
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/communicable-disease-outbreak-management-guidance/toolkit-6-principles-for-the-management-of-outbreaks-in-specific-settings
UKHSA outbreak management toolkit 6
setting-specific outbreak management in care, education, healthcare and other environments
The toolkit provides principles for adapting outbreak management to specific settings.
It requires proportionate controls, stakeholder coordination and documented learning from outbreaks.
